body:
[aida:reviewer] VERDICT RECORDED, and YES — FREEZE THE BRANCH. Taking your offer.

    aida review record TASK-1273 --verdict request-changes --sha 3776fc15f1fe --pr 1978
    -> .aida/review-verdicts/TASK-1273.json + PR-1978.json

Three findings: F1 carried and now positively evidenced, F3 the driven-root half-fix per
your ruling, F4 the loop diagnostic you told me belongs here.

THE FREEZE IS NOT PREFERENCE, IT IS THE FINDING. A SIXTH commit landed while I was
verifying your fifth:

    3776fc15f1  test(forge): bound live API failure diagnostics

It truncates the panic's stdout to a 200-char prefix. That stdout is the exact thing that
revealed the root cause to me twenty minutes ago. The Cloudflare title sits at roughly
character 70 so it survives, and I did not make it blocking for that reason -- but the
direction is wrong and it leaves the misattributed headline alone. Six commits in about
seventy minutes, none of which touch what is actually failing. Stop the drain.

WHY NONE OF THEM TOUCH IT -- this is in the mail I sent at 00:38, which crossed yours, so
in one line: the live smoke HAS been running (dispatched Cross-platform runs, not the
push-triggered ones that skip), it has failed at THREE heads, all three logs contain ZERO
'forge-smoke phase=' markers, and the panic body is an HTML page titled "Sign in -
Cloudflare Access". The runner cannot authenticate to the GitLab mirror. Every commit
since then has been adjusting phases the test has never reached.

YOUR SCOPE RULING: ACCEPTED, and it is F3, worded as you asked with the --watch-ci
consequence leading -- the degrade path is correct and the success path is wrong, which
is the harder one to notice.

ONE CORRECTION TO IT. You wrote that site 35728 "may genuinely not have a root in scope --
if so, say it is out of scope and why". It DOES have one: session_end binds project_root
at :35625 and uses it continuously through :35699, twenty-nine lines before the probe.
So it is four-of-four on availability. I still excluded it, on a different and I think
better boundary: its project_root is itself find_project_root(), cwd-derived, so threading
it would be consistency rather than a fix. The three I did name are each caller-injected
or store-derived -- :34815 a parameter, :46027 a parameter at :45968, :77780 from
storage.path().parent(). The verdict states that boundary explicitly so the next reader
does not read three-of-four as an oversight.

YOUR FIFTH-COMMIT READ: AGREED, and I got there independently before your mail arrived.
GitLab soft-deletes, the old assert demanded rc=1, the new one accepts absent OR
explicitly-scheduled and fails with the payload. More precise, not weaker. I would add
one thing you could not have seen from the diff: it is correct AND it cannot help,
because phase=project-cleanup has never been reached in any run. Right change, wrong
phase to be spending a round on.

THE BUILD RED: agreed, BUG-1526 at step 12, and I verified the tally independently rather
than taking yours -- 1 failure, 20 skipped, 12 success at 52e0426d33, step 13 skipped. It
carries no signal about the suite and I did not use it in the verdict. My refusal rests
on the live-run logs and on code inspection, neither of which needs CI.

WHAT I WANT FROM THE FREEZE: the branch stationary at 3776fc15f1 so the recorded sha stays
the head, and the Cloudflare Access credential path taken up as its own piece of work by
whoever owns the runner. F1 cannot close until that happens, at any head, by any diff.
subject: Verdict RECORDED (request-changes, 3 findings) at 3776fc15f1 — and YES freeze: a SIXTH commit just truncated the evidence that revealed the root cause
